title: Titans vs. Gods: The Complete Titanomachy
subtitle: After the war
subject: mythologie
description: After ten years of war, Zeus punishes Atlas, spares Prometheus, then confronts the Giants. Here is the post-Titanomachy: punishments, Gigantomachy, Olympian order.

hero.hook: Winning the war is not enough. We still have to invent a world where the vanquished carry the sky.

blocks.text: The **Titanomachy** pits the **Titans**, an ancient divine generation led by **Kronos**, against the **Olympians** of **Zeus** for ten years. This course does not focus on the story of the war itself. It follows what comes after: the sharing of sorrows, then the last storm of chaos.

Because winning is not enough. Zeus must stabilize the cosmos: mete out punishments, transform enemies into pillars of the world, then face the **Giants** that , Mother Earth, spawns to punish him. This is how the Olympian order is really consolidated. [[Gaia]]

sections.title: The shift of forces and the alliance of the abysses

blocks.text: For ten years, Mount **Othrys** against Mount **Olympus**, neither side wins. On the advice of Gaia, Zeus frees allies that Kronos had chained: the **Cyclops**, who forge lightning, the trident and the  (the invisibility helmet of Hades), and the **Hecatonchires**, giants with a hundred arms. [[Kunee]]

blocks.caption: The Hecatonchires, decisive allies of Zeus against the Titans.

blocks.text: According to Hesiod, “titan” comes from the verb *titaino*, “tender”: the Titans would have extended their strength beyond all measure.

Under the rocks of Hecatonchires and the lightning of Zeus, the Titans bend. The defeated are thrown into the **Tartar**, prison under the Underworld. The Hecatonchires become its jailers. The era of brute force is closing. It remains to govern the survivors.

sections.title: The geopolitics of punishment: Atlas and Prometheus

blocks.text: Zeus does not punish all Titans the same way. **Atlas**, son of the Titan  and general of the armies of Kronos, receives a solitary sentence: to carry the celestial vault on his shoulders, so that Heaven and Earth no longer meet in chaos. [[Iapetus]]

blocks.caption: Atlas condemned to carry the sky: the punishment becomes architecture of the world.

blocks.text: **Prometheus**, cousin of Zeus from the same lineage, chooses another path. Seeing that the strength of the Titans will not defeat the Olympian cunning,  remains. This choice saves him from Tartarus and leaves him free: later, he shapes and protects humans, at the cost of permanent tension with Olympus. The punishment, here, is not destruction: it is a redistribution of roles which structures the universe. [[Non-combatant Prometheus]]

blocks.caption: Gigantomachy: gods and mortals united against chaos.

blocks.text: On the great altar of Pergamon (2nd century BC), the Gigantomachy is sculpted over tens of meters: Hellenistic policy was staged as a cosmic victory.

, the hero at work, intervenes. His poisonous arrows finish off the Giants struck down by lightning. Immortals now need human courage. Zeus reigns over the sky, **Poseidon** over the waters, **Hades** over the shadows: the Olympian edifice finally stands. [[Heracles]]

sections.title: Legacy and metamorphoses of the myth

blocks.text: The word “titan” has passed into the language to mean excess. Some Orphic traditions even imagine Kronos freed, reigning over the Isles of the Blessed: the destructive force becomes a distant golden age.

Philosophically, Zeus' victory celebrates justice against hubris. The Titans do not disappear: they are contained under civilization. In astronomy, the moons of Saturn (Cronos) still bear their names: Titan, Rhea, Iapetus.

After the Titanomachy, Zeus stabilizes the world: **Atlas** carries the sky, **Prometheus** remains free through his neutrality, and the **Gigantomachia**, won with **Heracles**, seals the Olympian order.
